board: YL-90 AT24C256 I2C EEPROM module (red, 4-pin header VCC/GND/SCL/SDA, 10k pull-ups, address 0x50)
reason: Check passed on ESP32 and Pico (spec, wiring, design checks, breadboard, simulator, PCB DRC clean, footprint, LCSC). Modelled as an i2c-device with 16-bit word addresses; the driver splits writes at 64-byte page boundaries and waits out tWR with ACK polling per the datasheet. The EEPROM has no sliders, so the test checks a write/read round trip, not set controls. The simulator does not model in-page write wrap or the busy NACK, and the correct driver never relies on either.
